title: openai-compat: tool_choice semantics + schema mapping + tool message formatting
author: Priya Desai
description:
Motivation: upstream OpenAI-style function/tool calling has three areas where Redwood's compatibility layer was underspecified for our serving/runtime semantics: (1) tool_choice semantics when a model suggests a tool by name/index rather than emitting a full function call, (2) mapping OpenAI JSON Schemas to Redwood's ToolInput schemas to enable server-side validation and routing, and (3) consistent tool message formatting and streaming behavior so that tool outputs are delivered to clients and logged correctly. Summary: this PR implements canonical tool_choice handling (name/index resolution and deterministic disambiguation), a schema mapping layer that converts OpenAI-style JSON Schema to our internal tool contract, and updates message formatting plus streaming glue so tool invocations are emitted as explicit tool messages (role: "tool") and streamed reliably. Changes include API surface flags, docs, migration notes, tests, and integration fixes for the Kubernetes-based streaming proxy. Checklist:
- [x] Implement tool_choice resolution and deterministic fallback rules
- [x] Add schema_mapper module with bidirectional mapping and validation hooks
- [x] Ensure streaming emits tool call tokens and tool response messages in correct order and with stable backpressure handling
- [x] Update compatibility header X-OpenAI-Compat-Version and document behavior
- [x] Add unit/integration tests for ambiguous tool names, schema coercion, and streaming edge cases
- [x] Update docs (openai-compat/README + migration guide)
- [x] Run perf regressions; address a minor 5% tail latency uplift by batching tweak
- [x] Manual QA with redwood-quickstarts/tooling example (verified)

Technical details (single-string description; details in changed files): The new tool_choice resolver accepts either a numeric index (OpenAI numeric choice), an exact tool name, or a fuzzy match. Disambiguation rules: exact name > exact alias > index > fuzzy match, with deterministic tie-break on lexicographic order. If a resolved tool is not registered for the tenant, we now return a structured assistant message with an error_code and a tool-suggestion list rather than silently failing or falling back to a generic assistant response. Schema mapping: the schema_mapper converts OpenAI-style JSON Schema types (string/integer/array/object/enum/pattern) to Redwood ToolInput field descriptors (type, enum, constraints, examples). It supports coercion for common cases (string -> number when numeric string provided) and exposes validation errors as structured diagnostics so clients can surface them. Message formatting: tool invocations are emitted to clients as a streaming "tool_call" control event followed by the tool call payload; tool responses are emitted as role: "tool" messages and also written into the conversation history with metadata: tool_name, tool_version, invocation_id. Streaming fixes: resolved a race where tool output streaming could interleave with model fallback content due to incorrect half-close semantics in the proxy. We now add a per-invocation sequence ID and backpressure window to the proxy plus a small buffering window to ensure stable ordering under load. API surface: added header X-OpenAI-Compat-Version (value: "v1.2-rc1") to opt-in to the new tool_choice semantics and tool message formatting; default behavior remains backward compatible for requests without the header for this release. Tests & CI: added unit tests for schema mapping and tool_choice disambiguation, integration test that spins up the streaming proxy and a fake tool; CI matrix updated to run the integration test in the compatibility job. Migration notes: for customers who rely on older behavior (implicit assistant fallback), set header X-OpenAI-Compat-Version: legacy for now. See openai-compat/MIGRATION.md for details. Impact/Risks: small surface-area change; main risk is behavioral change for clients that parse model outputs expecting inlined assistant content rather than structured tool messages. We added telemetry to monitor for clients hitting fallback paths and defaulted the compatibility header to off. Rollout plan: feature-gated; staged rollout to hosted API customers, followed by Dedicated and Private after customer opt-in.

release_notes: OpenAI compatibility: improved tool calling support. Adds deterministic tool_choice resolution, JSON Schema -> Redwood tool schema mapping, and stable streaming for tool messages. Opt-in via X-OpenAI-Compat-Version=v1.2-rc1. See MIGRATION.md for details.
